issue.title: Triggerer restarts after a transient metadata database disconnect
issue.body:
On Airflow 3.2.2 (Python 3.12, PostgreSQL), a brief interruption to the metadata database connection caused the triggerer to exit and its pod to restart during `Trigger.clean_unused()`.

This issue is also present on `main` at commit [`194e0ea4`](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/194e0ea4c9890a7eed1b6df19eb72159f3e44841/airflow-core/src/airflow/models/trigger.py#L233): `Trigger.clean_unused()` retries its UPDATE using `run_with_db_retries()`, which does not roll back the session between attempts. After a connection loss invalidates the transaction, the next attempt reuses that invalid transaction and raises `PendingRollbackError`.

PR [#70961](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/70961) may address this incident because its cleanup retries use a fresh database session for each attempt.

comments.body: I would like to take a stab at this.

Minimal fix raised: #74650. It adds `session.rollback()` on `DBAPIError`/`StaleDataError` inside the existing `run_with_db_retries()` block in `Trigger.clean_unused`, matching the pattern already used by `retry_db_transaction` in `airflow/utils/retries.py`. 2-file change, +57/-8, with a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it.

For maintainer awareness: #70961 is an in-review PR that batches `clean_unused`. Its restructure to `with create_session(scoped=False)` per retry attempt would incidentally close this issue as a side effect, because each attempt gets a fresh session. So there are two viable paths:

1. Merge #74650 now as a targeted fix, independent of the batching PR's review timeline.
2. Treat this issue as subsumed by #70961 and close #74650 as redundant once #70961 lands.

Happy either way — flagging the overlap so reviewers can pick without duplicate effort. Cross-reference comment posted on #70961 as well.
